text:
deploy-bot: scheduled rollout: runtime v1.14 -> starting 2026-04-01T02:00:00Z, change window 2h, phased by region (EU then NA). Canary: 5% for first 15m. Pin fallback: v1.13 (read-only).

sara.nguyen: heads-up — support needs statuspage + customer email ready before canary. can we get a compact status snippet and rollback wording? :eyes:

kevin.choi: rolling out EU first as discussed. rollback criteria: >5% 5xxs over 10m OR median p95 latency regressed by >200ms for two consecutive 5m windows. if triggered, immediate pin to v1.13 and abort further regions.

lina (support): thanks. drafting statuspage snippet now. suggest both short public blurb and a more detailed ops note for customers on paid plans. will post preview here.

ben (sre): a few operational notes: ensure autoscale ramp disabled for canary group, KV cache warming off for canary to keep comparability. I'll run a quick smoke 10m before canary start.

sara.nguyen: status page (public):
```
Maintenance: Rolling runtime update (v1.13 -> v1.14) starting 2026-04-01 02:00 UTC. Short-lived canary in EU then phased rollout. Some requests may fall back to a previous version if we detect regressions. We expect minimal disruption.
```

sara.nguyen: status page (detailed/customer note):
```
What we're doing: Gradual rollout of runtime v1.14 to improve throughput and token cost. Canary (5%) in EU for 15m, then expand to NA.
Why you might notice it: We will pin to v1.13 automatically if we observe increased errors or latency regressions. Customers on Dedicated/Private will be notified individually if pinned.
If you rely on strict latency SLOs: we recommend temporarily routing critical routes to Dedicated pools during the 2h change window.
```

lina (support): customer email subject suggestion: "Planned runtime update — brief maintenance window (Apr 1)"

lina (support): customer email body draft:
```
Hello —
We will perform a planned, phased update of our inference runtime (v1.13 -> v1.14) on 2026-04-01 at 02:00 UTC. The update will be rolled out in phases (EU then NA) with a short canary. We expect no interruption for most customers. In the unlikely event of regressions, we will automatically revert affected traffic to v1.13 to minimize impact.

What to expect:
- Window: 02:00–04:00 UTC
- Possible brief fallbacks to earlier runtime for affected traffic
- We'll post live updates to status.redwood.ai during the window

If you have high-availability constraints or dedicated latency commitments, reply to this thread or open a ticket and we can discuss targeted routing for the window.

Thanks,
Redwood Support
```

sara.nguyen: kevin — can you confirm the exact status.redwood.ai permalink for the post after you create it? i'll queue the email once i have the link.

kevin.choi: will publish the status page entry 30m before start. permalink: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/rv1-2026-04-01 (preview pending). I'll also add the rollback bullet and a line about automatic pinning.

ben (sre): on-call will monitor dashboards; if rollback happens i'll post the deploybot rollback event here with timestamp so support can push immediate customer DMs.

lina (support): added reaction :thumbsup: to drafts. queuing final send time 01:25 UTC.

deploy-bot: canary started (2141599365) — 5% traffic EU. monitor: link: https://deploys.redwood.ai/run/2141598765/canary (auto-updates).

kevin.choi: smoke looks clean at +10m. p95 stable, error rate flat. continue to expand to 25% EU.

sara.nguyen: queued statuspage publish for 01:30 UTC (30m before). email scheduled to go at 01:25 UTC.

lina (support): ready to send targeted messages for any affected Dedicated customers if ben flags.

ben (sre): noted. standing by.

deploy-bot: expand to 25% EU (2141599620).

kevin.choi: no regressions after 30m, proceeding to NA canary at 5% in 15m. will post updates here.

sara.nguyen: thanks team — keeping thread for post-mortem notes if anything odd shows up. :pray:
